findings.finding: A new SCHEDULE 13D — control or activist intent, not a passive 13G — was accepted 2026-07-09T21:02:45 by self-filer CIK 0001734341, sixteen minutes before a Form 4, two days after an item 5.02 8-K (2026-07-07T20:16), and four days before director Daniel Englander bought $398k of stock in a single open-market purchase that raised his holding 117%; after those Form 4s on 2026-07-13/14 the company then filed nothing at all for seven weeks until the print itself.
findings.adversary_note: The claim is built from filings.json metadata, and the same metadata read one line further undercuts the activist framing. The 13D was accepted 2026-07-09T21:02:45 -- eighty-four seconds after a Form 3 (accession 0001231919-26-000745, accepted 2026-07-09T21:01:21) and two days after an 8-K carrying item 5.02, a director-or-officer change the company announced itself (accession 0001628280-26-047499, accepted 2026-07-07T20:16:11). A Form 3 is an initial statement of beneficial ownership by a new insider. A >5% holder who becomes a director files a Form 3 and converts to a 13D in the same minute, because board representation removes passive eligibility. That sequence is the ordinary signature of a company-disclosed board appointment, not of an unnoticed control raid, and the company-disclosed leg is the 8-K two days earlier. The tape then behaves as if it was noticed: 2026-07-08 close 4.93 -> 07-09 5.06 (+2.64% on 1,341,500 shares against a ~740k 20-day average) -> 07-13 5.21 -> 07-14 5.43, which is +4.22% on 1,637,900 shares, 2.2x average, on exactly the day the Englander Form 4 hit (accepted 2026-07-14T00:33:39). That is +10.1% over four sessions on double volume in the window the finding says nothing could react to, followed by a drift to 6.77 by 2026-08-31 (+33.8% from the 13D date, run_up_20d +19.19%, +102.69% off the 52-week low). And the surrounding context the finding says makes it matter is itself published in the capture: docs/601a3e5ab27afe4e9bca5545757b06c38a19f530.txt (admissible snapshot 20260830T083646Z) carries the insider buy as a dated roundup entry -- '$YEXT -- $398K single buy by insider Daniel Englander, +117% stake increase (Jul 13)' with a filingtracker link -- plus the $50m at 10.25% borrowed to buy back stock (message 2026-06-12) and the CEO's withdrawn $9-per-share proposal alongside the $150m authorisation (message 2026-02-02, with a news URL). What genuinely is not in the corpus is the 13D's holder, its size and its stated intent, because no body is stored -- that part is reachable-but-undrawn and it is why this is not in the seventies. Set against that, the mechanism does not route through this print: a control-intent stake and a possible renewed bid are a standing situation eight weeks old, not an FQ2 datapoint, so even the unpublished residual has no particular reason to resolve on 2026-09-01.

findings.finding: In an 2026-08-18 interview on a low-distribution VC newsletter, CEO Nikesh Arora says Anthropic's 'Mythos' model — disclosed 2026-04-07 and withheld from public release because it was too good at finding high-severity OS and browser vulnerabilities — has for the first time in his eight years put security in front of CEOs rather than CISOs ('Every CEO wants to talk about Mythos'), and he puts Mythos-level offensive capability roughly three months from being available in the wild, i.e. inside the FY27 guidance window he was about to set on 2026-09-01.
findings.adversary_note: The document the finding rests on refutes the finding's own distribution and novelty premises, and it does so in the stored body. First, distribution: the claim describes 'a low-distribution VC newsletter' showing '23 likes and 1 comment', but docs/6488c57c78f2f4950f8ff88c17ce80240313453e.txt embeds the X clips that carried these exact quotes -- the 'For 8 years I spent my career trying to convince CEOs' clip posted 2026-08-17T14:18 with 21.2K views, 126 likes, 13 reposts, and the same body records a 43,234-impression clip and a second at 9.84K views. The publisher's own schema block lists 10,000 subscribers. That is an order of magnitude more reach than the 23-like figure, and it landed 2026-08-17, two weeks before the print. Second, novelty of the three-month clock: the body itself sources it to earlier public remarks -- 'Speaking on All-In in June, Arora said a 6-week test surfaced vulnerabilities that would have taken his own team 5 to 7 years to find... He has also put Mythos-level offensive capability roughly 3 months from being available in the wild.' The All-In appearance is not a low-distribution channel, and the corpus separately carries https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/02/palo-alto-ceo-customer-meeting-requests-surged-ai-security-concerns.html in snapshot 20260830T154524Z -- CNBC, 2026-06-02, headlining the same CEO saying customer meeting requests surged on AI security concerns, which is the buying-centre-moves-up mechanism on a top-tier outlet three months early. Third, the corpus shows the mechanism as retail consensus the day before the print: the $PANW Stocktwits thread, docs/2cd9ab60291e7af8e0b7859d0643e7d7793a7a9c.txt, message 2026-08-31T18:44:26Z, states it almost verbatim -- 'It started with Mythos from Anthropic a few months ago... it can be only a matter of 1 to 3 months from now that everyone has access to such a model of Mythos like. And that means alarm of Cyber attacks screaming more demand for their Security... those stocks should surge.' A fourth corpus item, docs/7657b6ede74593aefa0dde340f51d274612fe05a.txt, carries '5 Cybersecurity Stocks Most Likely to Benefit as AI Threats Drive Budget Increases in 2026', which describes the Mythos Preview and Project Glasswing naming Palo Alto, bylined '4 months ago' i.e. around the 2026-04-07 disclosure. Fourth and worst for the finding: the source's own subtitle is '$PANW | 3X Mythos Run-up to $300B Market Cap' and its text says the company has gone '3x in value since Feb 2026' with Arora's explanation of the run-up being 'that is his explanation for why the sector has been bid up'. The publication being cited as unpriced colour says in its dek that the Mythos narrative already tripled the stock. The tape agrees at the margin too: 2026-08-26 339.31 -> 2026-08-27 382.85 is +12.8% on 7.31m shares against a 5.68m 20d average, four sessions before the print, in a window whose captured copy ties it to CrowdStrike's Q2 (fxleaders, 2026-08-27, in snapshot 20260830T154524Z). What remains unpublished elsewhere is one quotation's wording, not a number that changes the FY27 NGS ARR guide the corpus itself calls 'the key test'.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-04 a federal jury in Boston (Judge Patti Saris) returned the first Covidien hernia-mesh bellwether verdict against Medtronic — $88m, $77m to Larry Patterson and $11m to his wife, on failure-to-warn over Symbotex mesh, with no punitives and no fraud finding — and that verdict sits on top of roughly 2,400 federal MDL cases, about 7,450 Massachusetts state cases and a coordinated Minnesota action with no global settlement in place.
findings.adversary_note: The verdict is published inside the admissible corpus by two separate publishers and the bars show the market absorbing it and going up. The finding's own source (docs/893b8caad61d5614d48335b85cebe444a3c36817.txt, from admissible snapshot 20260830T152925Z) is a dated 2026-08-04 page that carries every number in the claim -- the $88m split $77m/$11m, no punitives, no fraud, the ~2,400 federal MDL / ~7,450 Massachusetts / Minnesota coordinated action counts, and the 'no global settlement' framing. So the case-count leg the hunter treats as the size of the tail is in the same public document as the headline, not one step beyond it. Independently, the Star Tribune story on the same federal bellwether appears twice in the capture: as a URL in snapshot 20260830T152925Z's skipped list, and as a link posted to the $MDT Stocktwits feed on 2026-08-09 (docs/dd07807b1a0282e03d16c9e4a92a1ce97869b713.txt, fetched 2026-08-30T08:36:22Z from admissible snapshot 20260830T083620Z). That is a metro daily in the company's home market plus retail circulation, three weeks before the print. The tape then says what the market did with it: 2026-08-03 close 86.68 -> 08-04 (verdict day) 86.20, -0.55% on 6.36m shares against a 6.84m 20d average, i.e. a nothing day; 08-07 +1.44% and 08-10 +2.58%; and by 08-19 the stock was 94.13, +9.2% from the verdict close. The information was out and the stock rose through it. Arithmetic supports that being rational rather than an oversight: $88m is 0.076% of the $115.16bn market cap in event.json, and even a full-docket provision at Bard-like per-claim economics across ~9,850 cases is under 1% of cap, arriving as a 10-Q contingency footnote rather than in an FQ1 P&L. What the corpus genuinely does not contain is any sell-side or preview note sizing the aggregate, which is why this is not a 90.

findings.finding: FDA issued an Early Alert on Medtronic's and Given Imaging's Bravo esophageal pH monitoring capsule delivery device: Medtronic sent affected customers a quarantine letter on 2026-08-06 and, as of 2026-08-10, had reported 184 serious injuries and no deaths, and separately removed the Harmony pulmonary valve delivery catheter system after a 2026-05-28 customer letter over tip detachment.
findings.adversary_note: This one is in the captured trade press under a headline that is the claim, and it is in the price bars on the day it became public. MedTech Dive published 'Medtronic recalls pH monitoring capsule linked to 184 serious injuries' on 2026-08-28 (docs/2edb580f0dd2d292f6dec88e4ab4151efd4c407e.txt: schema datePublished 2026-08-28T12:56:00, byline 'Published Aug. 28, 2026', body 'As of Aug. 10, Medtronic had received reports of 184 serious injuries and no deaths'), and it is item sha 2edb580f in the admissible snapshot 20260830T152925Z. The primary FDA page in the same snapshot carries its own dates: schema datePublished 'Thu, 08/27/2026' and 'Content current as of: 08/27/2026'. So the hunter's source_date of 2026-08-10 is the injury-count as-of date, not the publication date -- the alert went public on 2026-08-27, five sessions before the print, not three and a half weeks. On that exact date the stock fell 92.02 -> 89.97, -2.23% on 7.77m shares against a 6.84m 20d average, the largest single down day in the whole admissible window and about 1.7x a one-day move at the baseline's 21.3% realised vol. I state that as consistency rather than proof of causation, but the date match is exact and it is the only candidate news on the tape. The Harmony leg is published in the corpus too: its own FDA page (sha a866ba69) and MedTech Dive 825186 'Medtronic recalls heart valve delivery catheter for risk of tip detaching' are both admissible items in the same snapshot. On size the finding concedes the point -- Bravo is immaterial to revenue against a $115bn cap -- so the residual is a product-liability seed that cannot land in an FQ1 print. Not 95 only because no sell-side note in the admissible corpus connects the alert to the quarter's numbers.

findings.finding: The market had already fully reacted to this print before the filing that defines it: the results release and earnings call landed pre-open on 2026-09-01, the stock fell from a 2.89 prior close to 2.34 by 11:06 ET on 43.8m shares against a 19.8m twenty-day average, and closed at 2.39 — near the low — while the 6-K carrying the actual financial statements was not accepted until 20:52 UTC (16:52 ET), which puts the detailed disclosure inside the measured window rather than before it.
findings.source: no URL in corpus; kind: social, stocktwits $RZLV thread fetched 2026-09-01T15:06:04Z, cross-checked against seal.json and quote.json
findings.adversary_note: I concede the observation and score it high because the observation is that the move already happened -- it is a statement about the price, made from the price. Everything in it is arithmetic on two machine-generated files in the capture, both of which the resolver reads as well: seal.json gives accepted_utc 2026-09-01T20:52:42Z (16:52 ET) for accession 0001193125-26-378541, and quote.json's final bar gives 2.34 on 43,813,931 shares at a 15:06:04Z fetch against avg_volume_20d 19,786,510. Prior close 2026-08-31 was 2.89, so 2.34 is -19.03% by 11:06 ET, and the baseline's run_up_5d_pct of -19.26% is 2.39/2.96 from the 2026-08-25 close, i.e. the baseline books the reaction as run-in. That is a correct and useful catch about window specification, and I say so plainly. But as a claim about information it is worth nothing directional: it asserts that the market has fully reacted, which is the definition of priced. Nothing about it is hidden, contested or unpublished -- the tape is the publication. My read of what the tape is showing: the fall IS the event, not a run-down I could retro-fit to any bearish thesis. The corpus supports that reading independently of the bars, because the only news-side item in the entire capture is a Stocktwits sweep whose messages between 14:22Z and 15:04Z discuss H1 results, the call, the cash position and the buyback in the past tense while quoting live prices of 2.32-2.33 -- results commentary, not anticipation. The residual I cannot price is whether the 6-K statements filed at 20:52Z produce a second leg on the following session, which is genuinely outside the tape I am allowed to read; that residual is the reason this is 92 and not 100.

findings.finding: On the 2026-09-01 call, disclosure quoted repeatedly in the pre-seal thread puts total cash at $100.5m but unrestricted cash at only $33.2m, against a roughly $300m buyback the company had announced, and management ended the call saying no online questions had been submitted — leaving the buyback and the 2027 outlook unaddressed — while H1 net loss was about $139m of which $67.5m was non-cash ($41.5m share-based comp, $20.4m D&A, $5.6m impairment).
findings.source: no URL in corpus; kind: social, stocktwits $RZLV thread fetched 2026-09-01T15:06:04Z
findings.adversary_note: Every number in this finding is in the corpus document it cites, published on the public $RZLV feed while the stock was collapsing on 2.2x volume, which makes it contemporaneously transacted rather than unpropagated. From docs/a6abeff7bb5c8e7a5f9bb05523161a9d6b9daaa6.txt: line 111, 2026-09-01T14:32:56Z -- 'Dilution Dan only has $33.2M unrestricted cash. He barely has enough to keep the lights on, much less buy back more shares'; line 49, 14:52:32Z -- 'total cash position safely sits at $100.5 million... $67.5 million of those losses were entirely non-cash... $41.5 million in share-based... $20.4 million in depreciation and amortization$5.6 million in asset impairment'; line 123, 14:29:48Z -- 'they said there were no online questions submitted on the conference call, and ended it immediately after... My questions were regarding the share buyback, and 2027 outlook'; line 124 -- '$300m buyback?'; line 10 -- 'Announcing a buy back that is 3x cash reserves is wild work'; line 52 -- 'Rezolve reports -139 million net for H1 alone'. The unrestricted-versus-total split, the loss, the non-cash bridge, the buyback ratio and the unanswered-questions detail are therefore all published pre-seal, in the capture, timestamped, and the conclusion the finding draws was drawn in public in the same hour: line 162, 14:22:56Z -- '1. The buyback is probably off the table. 2. There is probably more dilution coming'; line 75 -- 'DILUTION is coming!!!!!'. Meanwhile 43.8m shares changed hands by 11:06 ET against a 19.8m average and the price went 2.89 -> 2.34. So the mechanism was stated and the volume to price it was there. I do not concede fully, for two reasons that keep this off 90: the figures reach me only as retail paraphrase of a call, with no wire, sell-side or filing text in the capture to check them against, and the formal statements land at 20:52Z, after the close, so the balance-sheet detail gets its first authoritative reading inside the measured window rather than before it. The magnitude is also real -- a serial issuer with two F-3s and three prospectus supplements in ten months (filings.json: F-3 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-19, 424B7 2025-11-07, 424B3 2025-12-30, 424B5 2026-01-21) and $33.2m unrestricted against a $300m authorisation has one obvious next move, and on a $2.39 stock a raise is worth high single to low double digits in percent. That is why the size check is large and the priced-in number is nevertheless high: material, but published and traded in the same session.
